about: READ-ONLY: renders what `github-create-repository` WOULD create on GitHub, and changes nothing (infra/forge/github-act.sh create-repository --plan; design 76155676, backlog 6a8ff89f). It reads, as the GitHub App's installation on <owner> (the token slot /etc/boss-publish/github-app/<owner>.token the broker's installation token is rendered into), whether <owner> is an organisation (an installation token creates repositories only in one) and whether <owner>/<name> exists. Absent, the plan names the two acts — POST /orgs/<owner>/repos, empty (auto_init false), at the requested visibility, then PUT /repos/<owner>/<name>/actions/permissions {"enabled":false}, since GitHub enables Actions on every new repository (backlog e727fcfd) — and their proof. Standing exactly as declared (that visibility, not a fork, not archived), the plan reads its Actions permission too: disabled, it names no act; enabled, it names the PUT alone. A fork, the other visibility, an archived or moved repository, a non-organisation owner, or an unusable token slot is a refusal, exit 78, not a plan. No clock and no token in the bytes; its sha256 is printed on stderr as `plan-sha256:`, and that hash is what David's passkey signs (design 17835005 q1).
